fields.title: 1. GEICO Combined Ratio — Definition Fixed and A-2029-1 Made Judgeable
fields.md:
The SEC 10-Q segment note (XBRL R110) gives GEICO in four lines: revenues (earned premiums), losses and LAE, other segment items, and pre-tax underwriting earnings (USD millions; source below the table):

| GEICO | 3Q26 | 3Q25 |
|---|---|---|
| Earned premiums (Revenues) | 11,405 | 11,264 |
| Losses & LAE | 8,733 | 8,047 |
| Other segment items (expenses) | 1,690 | 1,444 |
| Total costs | 10,423 | 9,491 |
| Pre-tax underwriting earnings | 982 | 1,773 |
| Loss ratio (calculated) | 76.6% | 71.4% |
| Expense ratio (calculated) | 14.8% | 12.8% |
| Combined ratio (calculated = total costs ÷ earned premiums) | 91.4% | 84.3% |

Source: [10-Q segment note R110](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526452412/R110.htm) (2026-11-09). Calculation: 10,423 ÷ 11,405 = 91.4% · 9,491 ÷ 11,264 = 84.3%.

- **Definition fixed (state.definitions.geico_combined)**: Combined ratio = (losses & LAE + other segment items) ÷ earned premiums, based on the SEC segment note. This definition interlocks as an identity with 'pre-tax underwriting earnings = earned premiums × (1 − combined ratio)' (982 ÷ 11,405 = 8.6% = 100% − 91.4%, calculated) — so the figure is pinned down to a single number even if the company does not publish the ratio separately.
- The 84.5% reported in Round 1 (Forbes) cannot be reproduced for 3Q26 from any combination in the SEC filing. The closest value is **84.3% for 3Q25 a year earlier** (calculated) — possibly the report carried over the prior-year value or a different period (estimate). It is not used in the judgment.
- **A-2029-1 progress**: GEICO 3Q26 91.4% − Progressive 3Q26 88.7% ([Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/breaking-news/progressives-q3-profit-slips-3-despite-better-underwriting-margin-593580.aspx) 2026-10-15) = **+2.7%p** (calculated; the milestone is 0 or below). The status changes from undetermined to in progress. A year earlier, GEICO's 84.3% was 5.2%p lower than Progressive's 89.5% (prior-year figure from the same source) (calculated) — it gave up 7.9%p in one year (calculated 2.7 + 5.2).
- The 2.0%p rise in the expense ratio (14.8 − 12.8, calculated) is smaller than the rise in the loss ratio (+5.2%p, calculated 76.6 − 71.4) — most of the gap is losses after rate cuts (judgment, based on the table above). The signal for disruptive variable D1 has become clearer than in Round 1.
- Other insurance segments in the same note (calculated = total costs ÷ revenues): BH Primary 97.4% (4,503 ÷ 4,622; prior year 89.3% = 4,205 ÷ 4,711) — pre-tax underwriting earnings 119 (prior year 506). BHRG includes life and annuity benefits (1,125), so it is not read as a combined ratio (source: [R110](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526452412/R110.htm)).
- R1 (GEICO quarterly loss ratio above 78% for two consecutive quarters): not met at 76.6% in 3Q26 — remains on hold (calculation in the table above).
